results.title: CMS Transmittal 1875 - Consultation service codes no longer recognized for Medicare payment
results.text:
# Medicare consultation code elimination, January 1, 2010

## Policy change

Effective January 1, 2010, Medicare stopped recognizing consultation service codes 99241-99245 and 99251-99255 for Part B payment under the physician fee schedule. The change was applied budget-neutrally across inpatient and office/outpatient settings, with limited exceptions for telehealth consultation G-codes.

## Rationale

CMS restructured evaluation and management (E/M) payment. The transmittal states that the agency increased the work relative value units (RVUs) for new and established office visits and increased payment for initial hospital and nursing facility visits. These increased values were also carried into practice expense and malpractice calculations and into the E/M component of global surgical codes.

## What to bill instead, by setting

with reassigned billing rights. Rural Health Clinics and Federally Qualified Health Centers: consultation codes were discontinued in favor of office visit codes (99201-99215) and nursing facility codes (99304-99306) as appropriate. ## Documentation

All E/M services must meet existing E/M documentation guidelines. Services should be documented during or immediately after they are provided. Code selection should reflect the actual service content.

## Timeline

The effective date was January 1, 2010, and implementation was January 4, 2010. The transmittal removed all references to consultation codes from Claims Processing Manual Chapter 12, Section 30.6.

Critical Access Hospital Method II: appropriate new or established visit codes (99201-99215) are reported on type of bill 85X with revenue codes 96X, 97X or 98X for physicians and nonphysician practitioners with reassigned billing rights.

Rural Health Clinics and Federally Qualified Health Centers: consultation codes were discontinued in favor of office visit codes (99201-99215) and nursing facility codes (99304-99306) as appropriate.

final_text:
Claim 1219093 is an outpatient claim. The model gives it a denial probability of 0.9456, against a validation-set average of 0.1805. That is 5.24 times the average, or 76.5 percentage points higher. The denial label in this project is synthetic, so this is the probability of a constructed label and not of a real payer decision.

**What the model weighs:** Almost all of the score comes from one feature, HCPCS_CD (the procedure or service code billed), with the value 99241. It adds 4.603 log-odds, which is an odds change of 9880 percent. The other features barely move the score:
- Principal diagnosis N184 adds 0.048.
- Billing provider 11T143 adds 0.035.
- Three features are undocumented in the project data dictionary: CARR_CLM_BLG_NPI_NUM, LINE_PLACE_OF_SRVC_CD and ICD_DGNS_CD1. Their effects are tiny.

**Policy context:** CMS Transmittal 1875 says that from January 1, 2010, Medicare stopped recognizing consultation codes 99241-99245 and 99251-99255 for Part B payment. The transmittal names office and outpatient visit codes 99201-99215 as the alternative for that setting. Codes are chosen by visit complexity and patient relationship, and the documentation must support the code.

**Before submitting, check:**
- Whether 99241 is the right code for this payer.
- Whether the payer expects an office or outpatient visit code instead.
- Whether the documentation supports the code you choose.

The policy documents don't cover the diagnosis or provider effects.
